### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.snippets

### Question

I'm not sure whether this belongs here or under `blink.cmp` so, apologies!

I'm trying to make blink and mini.snippets play nice with each other, which has been a bit of a journey. Here's my goal currently: 
 - disable all mini.snippet keybinds
 - set a blink keybind to either accept the current selection, or if none, call `MiniSnippets.expand()`

Here's what the keybinds look like in blink (I also set `snippets.preset = 'mini_snippets'`):
```
keymap = {
    preset = 'none',
    ['<C-j>']   = { 'select_next', 'fallback' },
    ['<C-k>']   = { 'select_prev', 'fallback' },
    ['<C-c>']   = { 'cancel', 'fallback' },
    ['<C-e>']   = {
        'accept',
        function ()
            MiniSnippets.expand()
        end
    },
    ['<Tab>']   = { 'snippet_forward', 'fallback' },
    ['<S-Tab>'] = { 'snippet_backward', 'fallback' },
 },
```

The issue is that, as in the title, I get error `E565` with a stacktrace pointing to mini, specifically 
```
in nvim_buf_set_text
... in mini: delete_region
... in mini: call_in_insert_mode
... in mini: insert
... in mini: select
... in mini: expand
... in blink: command
```

The (bigger??) issue is that I can't find a reproduction of this. I did a minimal `init.lua` which only installed blink and mini (and only set relevant parts of each) and the snippet expanded just fine! To be clear, when using this, I do not make a selection in the blink menu; I just type out the prefix and hit `<C-e>`. I also tried to find a single culprit by removing my other plugins one at a time, (though I added them back in before removing again because otherwise the number of combos to test gets... big) with no luck.

Am I calling `MiniSnippets.expand()` incorrectly? I tried with both `select` and `match` set to `false`, but no dice. Long story short, any leads are appreciated!

Editing to add some other simple things I tried:
 - deleting/rebuilding `.local/{share, state}/nvim`
 - adding a `return true` or `return false` to the `<C-e>` function
 - `require('mini.snippets').expand()` instead of `MiniSnippets.expand()`

Second edit to add the motivation:
When trying out the example snippets, (only!) "Choices" has a problem where the blink menu does not disappear. If I trigger the snippet through blink, however, the menu _does_ disappear. There's another issue where the choice menu is gigantic and includes a ton of extra stuff besides just `a|b`, but I think that's a separate issue. I figured I could just move the snippet expansion into the blink keymap to fix it. It might not work in the end, but I can't even test it to find out lol

comment_data.body:
Hello @rohrsben,

It's a bit difficult to help without seeing your full config for `blink` and `mini.snippets`.

As you are using `MiniSnippets.expand`, I *assume*:

1. You want `mini.snippets` to handle all snippets from the `lsp`, selected with `blink`
2. You don't want `blink` to present all other snippets. 

I do something similar when using `blink`, and there are some caveats indeed. See my config for [blink](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/b95deaec1f595c73c42234cce37ddbac33469030/lua/ak/editing/blink_completion.lua#L42) and [mini.snippets](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/b95deaec1f595c73c42234cce37ddbac33469030/lua/ak/editing/snippets.lua#L17).

EDIT: Could you add the following to the options for mini.snippet? 

```lua
-- ...
  expand = {
    select = function(snippets, insert)
        require("blink.cmp").cancel() -- cancel uses vim.schedule
        vim.schedule(function() MiniSnippets.default_select(snippets, insert) end)
    end,
  },
-- ...

```

reply_data.bodyHTML:
@echasnovski, what's your opinion?

This looks like a side effect of 'Saghen/blink.cmp' trying to do dot repeat. As choices are shown via built-in completion menu, it is totally reasonable that it can be affected by something hacky when trying to enable dot-repeat. The following config does not show the issue:

require('blink.cmp').setup({
  snippets = { preset = 'mini_snippets' },
  completion = {
    accept = {
      dot_repeat = false,
    },
  },
})

... no menu shows up until I hit (next option binding) and then I get a menu with seemingly... every possible completion in the buffer?

@rohrsben, a bit explanation about this. Choices are shown using built-in completion menu, which has hard-coded <C-n> and <C-p> to navigate to next and previous item respectively (see :h ins-completion-menu). However, if no menu is visible, those keys act as to start special built-in keyword completion (see :h i_CTRL-N and :h i_CTRL-P). That's why you see "every possible completion in the buffer", which in fact is probably a bit more than that and can be configured via :h 'complete'.

title: Getting error E565 when using MiniSnippets.expand()
